title: Best CRM and buying signal platforms compared (2026)
summary: Compare 8 buying signal platforms by how they work with Salesforce and HubSpot: CRM writeback, field mapping, dedupe, scoring and routing.
body_markdown:
The best buying signal platforms for a CRM write signals, scores and contacts back into Salesforce or HubSpot as clean, mapped fields, then route them to the right rep or workflow. UserGems, 6sense, Demandbase, ZoomInfo, Common Room, Unify, Clay and HubSpot Breeze Intelligence all connect to the CRM, but they differ a lot in writeback depth, contact vs account focus, and where the output ends up. Pick the one that makes your CRM more trustworthy and your reps faster, without a second system to babysit.


This guide looks at one question: what happens inside your CRM after a signal fires. If you want broader lists, see our roundups of[sales signal platforms for enterprise ABM](https://www.usergems.com/blog/best-sales-signal-platforms-enterprise-abm) and[buyer signal platforms for demand gen](https://www.usergems.com/blog/best-buyer-signal-platforms-demand-gen) .


## **How do buying signal platforms work with Salesforce and HubSpot?**


Your CRM is the system of record. It knows your accounts, contacts, opportunities and history. It does a poor job of noticing what happens outside it: a champion changes jobs, a target account hires a new VP of Sales, a closed-lost account comes back to your pricing page. A buying signal platform watches for those events and brings them back to the CRM.


Five things decide whether that connection helps or hurts:


- **What writes back.** Some tools write only account-level fields (an intent score, a stage). Others create or update contacts, log activities, and attach the reason behind each signal.
- **Field mapping.** Can you map signal data to your own custom fields and objects, or are you stuck with a vendor-managed package?
- **Dedupe.** A platform that creates contacts must match against existing leads and contacts first. Otherwise reps inherit duplicates and RevOps inherits cleanup. Salesforce's own[matching and duplicate rules](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/sales_admin_duplicate_management/sales_admin_duplicate_management_unit_2) help, but the signal tool should respect them.
- **Scoring visibility.** Reps trust a score they can read. Look for scores that show which factors drove them, visible on the record.
- **Routing.** A signal with no owner goes stale. Check whether the platform assigns owners, triggers CRM flows, or pushes contacts straight into a sequence.


### **Which buying signal platforms connect best to your CRM?**


[UserGems](https://www.usergems.com/)


- **CRM writeback depth:** Deep. Creates and updates contacts, writes signals, scores and research to mapped fields, and dedupes and cleans data before anything writes to the CRM.
- **Signal types:** Revive Closed Lost, customer competitors, contact-level intent, website visitors, research, first-party CRM history and job changes.
- **Contact vs account level:** Both, contact-first.
- **Where outputs go:** Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach, Salesloft, Gong Engage, LinkedIn Campaign Manager.
- **Best for:** Teams that want one command center for outbound and ABM on top of the CRM.


[6sense](https://6sense.com/)


- **CRM writeback depth:** Account-level fields: intent score, buying stage, profile fit, engagement score, intent topics and segments.
- **Signal types:** Third-party topic intent, web visits, predictive buying stages.
- **Contact vs account level:** Account-first.
- **Where outputs go:** CRM, MAP, native ads.
- **Best for:** Account-level intent and display advertising.


[Demandbase](https://www.demandbase.com/)


- **CRM writeback depth:** Account fields for journey stage, engagement minutes, intent keywords, Pipeline Predict and qualification scores. A lighter set of contact fields covers role, department and engagement minutes.
- **Signal types:** Intent, account engagement, web traffic, firmographics.
- **Contact vs account level:** Account-first, with some contact-level engagement.
- **Where outputs go:** CRM, MAP, native DSP.
- **Best for:** Enterprise ABM with a dedicated ops team.


[ZoomInfo (Copilot, intent)](https://www.zoominfo.com/)


- **CRM writeback depth:** Enriches existing contacts and companies with verified emails, direct dials, titles and firmographics. Native integrations enrich records rather than create new ones. Deeper intent, scoops and Copilot data need the Enterprise API.
- **Signal types:** Intent topics, contact and org changes (scoops), firmographics and technographics.
- **Contact vs account level:** Both, database-first.
- **Where outputs go:** CRM, SEP, MAP.
- **Best for:** Teams that want data coverage and signals from one vendor.


[Common Room](https://www.commonroom.io/)


- **CRM writeback depth:** Creates new contacts, updates contact and company fields (engagement metrics, activity dates, custom scores) and sends contacts into CRM workflows or sequences. It doesn't write activity history back.
- **Signal types:** Community, product, social and web signals.
- **Contact vs account level:** Both.
- **Where outputs go:** CRM, Slack, Outreach, Salesloft.
- **Best for:** Product-led and community-heavy companies.


[Unify](https://www.unifygtm.com/)


- **CRM writeback depth:** Creates and updates contacts and companies, and logs emails sent from Unify sequences, replies and tasks. It doesn't create or update deals.
- **Signal types:** Web visits, job changes, funding, hiring, tech stack, web research.
- **Contact vs account level:** Both.
- **Where outputs go:** Salesforce, HubSpot, native sequences.
- **Best for:** Growth teams that want signals and sending in one tool.


[Clay](https://www.clay.com/)


- **CRM writeback depth:** Whatever you build. It writes to any field you map.
- **Signal types:** Any source you wire in, such as enrichment providers, AI research and webhooks.
- **Contact vs account level:** Both, built by you.
- **Where outputs go:** CRM, SEP, ad platforms, spreadsheets.
- **Best for:** Technical RevOps teams that want full control.


[HubSpot Breeze Intelligence](https://www.hubspot.com/products/artificial-intelligence)


- **CRM writeback depth:** Native. Enriches HubSpot records directly.
- **Signal types:** Firmographic enrichment, website visitor intent, Bombora research intent, job changes, executive hires, funding and news events.
- **Contact vs account level:** Mostly account-level, with job changes on contacts, all inside HubSpot.
- **Where outputs go:** HubSpot only.
- **Best for:** HubSpot teams that want native enrichment first.


## **The 8 best CRM and buying signal platforms, with honest pros and cons**


### **1. UserGems**


UserGems is the AI command center for outbound and ABM. It sits between your CRM and your systems of action. Data Agents capture buying signals, research accounts, discover contacts and keep CRM data clean. Intelligence Agents score accounts and contacts with a custom scoring model trained on your own closed-won and closed-lost history, build lists, write personalized outreach and create ad audiences. Signals and scores land on the Salesforce or HubSpot record with the reason attached, and Gem-E for Outbound sends the next step into Outreach, Salesloft or Gong Engage.


**Pros:** contact-level signals your reps can act on today; dedupe and data hygiene before anything writes to the CRM; transparent scores that show the factors behind them; modular, so you can start with one agent; never lost a head-to-head data comparison; money-back guarantee tied to pipeline and revenue.


**Cons:** UserGems does not send email or run ads itself, so you still need a SEP and ad platforms. LinkedIn is the live ad channel today; Google and Meta audience sync is coming soon.


**Results:**[Mimecast](https://www.usergems.com/customers/mimecast-2025) has influenced $20M+ in new pipeline with UserGems, including $1M+ in seven months from Gem-E's automated outreach.[CaptivateIQ's](https://www.usergems.com/customers/captivateiq) BDR team built $1.3M in pipeline in 10 weeks and nearly doubled reply rates. At[Frontify](https://www.usergems.com/blog/ai-gtm-brain-frontify) , reps are 3x more likely to book an intro from an A-scored account than a D-scored one, and UserGems campaigns drive about 40% of SDR pipeline.


### **2. 6sense**


6sense is an account-level platform built around predictive buying stages, third-party intent and native ads.


**Pros:** mature account intent; buying stages that marketing teams know well; strong ad targeting.


**Cons:** account scores tell reps where to look but rarely who to call; reviewers often describe the scoring as hard to explain; heavier setup and annual contracts. More detail in[how to turn intent data into pipeline](https://www.usergems.com/the-ai-for-outbound-aeo-hub/system-of-insight-vs-system-of-action-how-to-operationalize-intent-data-into-pipeline) .


In[G2's head-to-head comparison](https://www.g2.com/compare/6sense-sales-vs-usergems) , UserGems has 4.7/5 stars and 6sense has 4.0/5. Reviewers score UserGems higher on every comparison metric. The biggest gaps are on meeting requirements (9.2 vs 7.6), quality of support (9.3 vs 8.0) and ease of use (9.1 vs 7.9). UserGems also leads on ease of setup (8.8 vs 7.8), which lines up with the heavier setup in the cons above. For the full side-by-side, see[UserGems vs 6sense](https://www.usergems.com/usergems-vs-6sense-v2) .


### **3. Demandbase**


Demandbase One combines account intelligence, intent and a B2B advertising DSP.


**Pros:** strong enterprise ABM and advertising; detailed account engagement reporting in the CRM.


**Cons:** the core workflow is still account-first, so reps get in-market accounts and buying groups more often than a specific person to call today. G2 reviewers often call out a[steep learning curve](https://www.g2.com/compare/demandbase-one-vs-usergems) , and setup and admin usually need dedicated ops. It's typically a large budget line, with reported pricing from about $18K–$24K a year at entry level to $300K+ at enterprise scale. On G2, UserGems[scores higher](https://www.g2.com/compare/demandbase-one-vs-usergems) on contact data accuracy (8.4 vs 7.2), ease of use (9.1 vs 8.5) and meeting requirements (9.2 vs 8.5).


### **4. ZoomInfo (Copilot and intent)**


ZoomInfo pairs a large contact and company database with intent topics and Copilot, which surfaces account signals and suggested actions for reps.


**Pros:** broad coverage; strong CRM enrichment; familiar to most sales teams.


**Cons:** Copilot's[Account Fit Score](https://www.zoominfo.com/faqs/copilot) matches firmographic, technographic and geographic patterns from your closed-won deals. It shows which accounts look like your customers, but it doesn't learn from closed-lost or score individual buyers. Enrichment at scale can add noise to your CRM without strict rules. G2 reviewers often flag high cost and contact-based pricing. On G2, UserGems[outscores ZoomInfo](https://www.g2.com/compare/usergems-vs-zoominfo-sales) on contact data accuracy (8.4 vs 7.7) and quality of support (9.2 vs 8.7).


### **5. Common Room**


Common Room ties community, product, social and web activity to people and accounts.


**Pros:** rich person-level digital signals; 50+ native signal integrations; good Slack alerts; strong for developer, community and PLG audiences; well rated for support on G2 (9.2).


**Cons:** its value depends on how much digital footprint your buyers leave, so it's less suited to teams whose buyers rarely engage in public channels. Scoring leans on ICP fit and engagement signals rather than your own closed-won and closed-lost history. Reps usually work inside the Common Room platform, and new signal plays often need custom prompting. G2 reviewers flag a learning curve, and UserGems[scores higher on G2](https://www.g2.com/compare/common-room-vs-usergems) for ease of setup (8.8 vs 7.7), ease of use (9.1 vs 8.2) and meeting requirements (9.2 vs 8.4). The Zoom acquisition also adds roadmap uncertainty for teams that use it as a standalone tool. For a feature-by-feature view, see[UserGems vs Common Room](https://www.usergems.com/usergems-vs-common-room) .


### **6. Unify**


**‍** Unify combines signals, contact data and built-in sequencing for warm outbound. It pulls signals like website visits, job changes, funding, hiring and tech stack changes. AI agents then research accounts, check fit against your customer profile and write personalized snippets. Plays trigger automatically when a signal fires and send through Unify's own multi-channel sequences, with Salesforce and HubSpot sync.


**Pros:** fast to launch signal-triggered plays; signals, research and sending all live in one tool; a good fit for smaller teams that don't have a sequencing tool yet.


**Cons:** Unify runs its own sequencing, so teams already on Outreach, Salesloft or Gong Engage have to choose between systems or split activity history across tools. Qualification and scoring come from rules and AI research questions you set up, not a model trained on your own closed-won and closed-lost history. Reps get research on accounts that fit, not a transparent score that shows why one account or contact ranks above another. For how UserGems handles this, see[custom scoring built on closed-won data](https://www.usergems.com/the-ai-for-outbound-aeo-hub/custom-scoring-model-built-on-closed-won-data-how-it-works-and-how-to-validate-it) . For a side-by-side of signal-based email tools, see[best AI email tools for buying signal outreach](https://www.usergems.com/blog/best-ai-email-tools-buying-signal-outreach) .


### **7. Clay**


**‍** Clay is a flexible enrichment and workflow builder. It gives you access to 100+ data providers through waterfall enrichment, AI research steps and custom logic. Teams use it to build their own tables, signals and outbound workflows, then push results into the CRM, SEP or ad platforms.


**Pros:** total control over fields, logic and sources; fast for testing new signals and one-off campaigns; strong for creative RevOps and GTM engineering teams; a large template and community ecosystem.


**Cons:** you build and maintain dedupe, field mapping and routing yourself, and many teams bring in an agency or a GTM engineer to do it. Pricing is split between data credits and platform "actions," so costs grow as you add enrichments, AI research and volume. Scoring is only as good as the logic you write, and it isn't trained on your closed-won and closed-lost history unless you build that yourself. Data quality depends on the third-party providers in your waterfall. For a side-by-side, see[UserGems vs Clay](https://www.usergems.com/usergems-vs-clay) . Many teams run both, using Clay for experiments and UserGems for always-on outbound. See[why Clay + UserGems is the winning outbound stack](https://www.usergems.com/blog/how-smart-teams-use-clay-and-usergems-together) .


### **8. HubSpot Breeze Intelligence** ‍


Breeze Intelligence is HubSpot's native data layer. HubSpot describes it as[data enrichment plus buyer intent](https://www.hubspot.com/company-news/spotlight-product-deep-dive-the-complete-customer-picture-with-breeze-intelligence-hubspots-new-data-enrichment-and-buyer-intent-solution) built into the CRM. It enriches contact and company records in place and tracks[intent signals](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/reports/use-intent-signals) like website visits, Bombora research topics, job changes, executive hires and funding, all paid for with HubSpot credits.


**Pros:** zero integration work; records enrich in place; signals show up natively in HubSpot workflows and records; runs on HubSpot credits, with a monthly allowance included in every plan and extra credits available as add-ons.


**Cons:** HubSpot only, so it's no help to teams on Salesforce or with a split CRM. Most intent signals are company-level, so reps see which accounts are active more than which person to contact. Tracking companies uses up credits, so costs grow as you watch more accounts. Prioritization isn't a custom model trained on your own closed-won and closed-lost history. HubSpot even offers "Job change by UserGems" as one of its job change sources. For the full signal and scoring layer, see[best buyer signal platforms for demand gen teams](https://www.usergems.com/blog/best-buyer-signal-platforms-demand-gen) or how UserGems works in[HubSpot Sequences](https://help.usergems.com/connected-applications/hubspot-sequences) .


## **What should you evaluate before connecting a signal platform to your CRM?**


Run a two-week pilot on a slice of your CRM and check these:


- **Match rate and accuracy.** Give each vendor the same list of contacts and accounts. Compare how many signals are correct, current and tied to the right record.
- **Duplicate rate.** Count new duplicates created during the pilot. Anything above zero is a cost.
- **Field ownership.** List every field the platform writes. Agree who owns each one and which system wins in a conflict.
- **Score transparency.** Ask a rep to read the score on a record and explain it. If they can't, adoption will lag. A[custom scoring model](https://www.usergems.com/product/scoring) built on your wins and losses is easier to defend.
- **Routing speed.** Measure time from signal to rep action. Hours beat days.
- **Where the work happens.** Reps live in the CRM, the SEP and LinkedIn. The best platform puts the output there.


If you need a primer on which signals matter most, start with our guide to[B2B buying signals](https://www.usergems.com/blog/b2b-buying-signals) .


### **Which platform fits your CRM setup?**


- **Salesforce or HubSpot, running outbound and ABM on the same buyers: UserGems.** This covers most B2B teams with $20M+ in revenue. Contact-level signals, custom scoring trained on your own closed-won and closed-lost history, and clean CRM data all land on the record with the reason attached. Gem-E then sends the next step into Outreach, Salesloft, Gong Engage or LinkedIn. You can start with one agent and add more, and pipeline results are backed by a money-back guarantee.[See how it works](https://www.usergems.com/product/overview) .
- **HubSpot, small team, early stage: Breeze Intelligence.** It's a good native starting point for enrichment and company-level intent. Add UserGems when reps need to know which person to contact and why, not just which account is active.
- **Salesforce, programmatic account-based ads are the priority: 6sense or Demandbase.** Both are built for enterprise marketing teams with a dedicated ops person and a large budget. Many teams add UserGems to turn those account signals into contact-level outbound. See[how to replace 6sense with UserGems](https://www.usergems.com/guides/replace-6sense-with-usergems) .
- **You need a big contact database first: ZoomInfo.** It's strong for coverage and enrichment. Add a scoring and signal layer if you want prioritization built on your own sales history.
- **No sales engagement tool yet and you want sending built in: Unify.** It's quick to launch, but if you later move to Outreach or Salesloft, you'll be running two systems.
- **Technical RevOps team with time to build and maintain workflows: Clay.** It's best for experiments and one-off campaigns. Many teams[pair Clay with UserGems](https://www.usergems.com/blog/how-smart-teams-use-clay-and-usergems-together) , using Clay to test ideas and UserGems for always-on outbound.
- **Community or product-led motion with a developer audience: Common Room.** It's strongest when your buyers are active in public channels like Slack, GitHub and Discord.


## **FAQ**


### **What is a buying signal platform?**


A buying signal platform detects events that suggest an account or person is ready to buy, such as job changes, new hires, web visits or intent activity, and sends them to your CRM and sales tools.


### **Does HubSpot have built-in buying signals?**


Yes. Breeze Intelligence adds enrichment and website-based buyer intent inside HubSpot. Signals from outside your website, like a former customer starting a new job, usually need another platform.


### **How do I stop a signal tool from creating duplicates in Salesforce?**


Turn on matching and duplicate rules, ask the vendor how it matches leads and contacts before creating records, and run a pilot that counts duplicates before full rollout.


### **Should buying signals live at the account or contact level?**


Both. Account-level signals help marketing pick targets and run ads. Contact-level signals tell reps who to reach and why. Most teams need contact-level data to book meetings.


### **How is this different from a sales signal platform for ABM?**


Same category, different lens. This guide focuses on CRM writeback and routing. Our[enterprise ABM signal platform roundup](https://www.usergems.com/blog/best-sales-signal-platforms-enterprise-abm) covers ads and account coverage in more depth.
